modalLead: Config is laid out the way you read it. Pages & tags is now Structure — pages, categories, finders and collections — and Tags has moved in with the other tag panels under Bookmarks, where a tag belongs. Appearance sits above Bookmarks in the rail. On the dashboard, adding a category moved from c to Shift + N, so every letter starts a search again. And a theme's own colour now glows under the cards, widgets and panels of almost every theme instead of a handful.

items.text: Pages & tags is called Structure, and it holds what its name says. Pages, categories, finders and smart collections — the shelves your collection stands on. A tag is not a shelf, so Tags left for Bookmarks, where Tag suggestions and Your rules already were. Links you handed out before today still land where they should.

Tags is a Bookmarks tab, between List and Tag suggestions. The same word cloud, the same filter, the same rename-everywhere and delete-everywhere — one tab away from the list it describes, instead of one section away.

Appearance sits above Bookmarks. Appearance, Structure and Behavior say what the dashboard is; Bookmarks is what it shows. The rail now opens with the first of those rather than burying it under the collection.
The tabs under Structure read like every other strip. They were lowercase beside Bookmarks' List and Tags. Now: Categories · Pages · Finders · Collections.

A finder's address is wide enough to read. Name, address and shortcut each took a third of the row, so the one long value — the search URL you check for %s — was cut off while a five-letter shortcut sat in a field three times its size.
A link to a Bookmarks tab opens that tab. Settings, Local copies and the rest all opened List, however the address read — and a reload dropped you back there too.

A section name no longer breaks across two lines in the rail. One wrapped button in a column of single-line buttons made the whole rail look ragged, and it happened sooner in languages whose words are longer. The full name is on hover.

Adding a category is Shift + N, and c searches again. A bare c added a category and kept the letter to itself, so no bookmark whose shortcut starts with c — CNN, CLOUD, CALIB — could be reached by typing it. Every letter starts a search now. The cheat sheet (!), the printable sheet and Help all say Shift + N.

Almost every theme now glows a little of its own colour under a raised surface. It was built for a handful of themes and 132 of the 222 were flat — every light theme among them. A dark theme lifts its cards, widgets and panels with a halo; a light one lets the accent sit in the shadow underneath, because light around a surface on paper reads as a smudge. Themes whose whole point is quiet — Nocturne Ink, Porcelain, Paper Ink, Bone China, Salt Flat — stay flat on purpose, and Depth → Flat still switches all of it off.

Config has the glow too, on the Classic layout. Its tiles and panels were flat there whichever theme you picked. They now carry the same accent as the rest of the app — the colour only, not the drop shadows Classic never had.
